root_cause.text: The QUERY_INFO branch in smb2_ioctl_query_info() fails to validate that the server-reported OutputBufferLength corresponds to data that actually fits within the received response buffer (rsp_iov[1].iov_len), enabling a malicious server to cause copy_to_user() to read beyond the buffer and leak adjacent kernel heap memory.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "it never verifies that the flexible-array payload actually fits within rsp_iov[1].iov_len." and "A malicious server can return OutputBufferLength larger than the actual QUERY_INFO response, causing copy_to_user() to walk past the response buffer and expose adjacent kernel heap to userspace." The patch adds a bounds check using struct_size(qi_rsp, Buffer, qi.input_buffer_length) > rsp_iov[1].iov_len to guard the copy.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to prevent buffer over-read when server's OutputBufferLength exceeds actual response length.
intent_record.what: Added a check after updating qi.input_buffer_length to verify that if it is greater than zero, the struct size of qi_rsp including buffer up to that length does not exceed the actual response iov length. If it does, set rc to -EFAULT and jump to out.
intent_record.how: This change prevents a potential buffer over-read or out-of-bounds access by ensuring the server-provided buffer length does not exceed the actual received response data. It returns an error to the caller if the response is too short.

This assignment directly uses the untrusted server-reported OutputBufferLength without any bounds check against the response buffer size, causing a subsequent copy_to_user() to read beyond the kernel heap buffer.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only compares the server-reported OutputBufferLength against the user-provided input buffer length, but does not validate that it fits within the actual response buffer (rsp_iov[1].iov_len). A malicious server can specify an oversized OutputBufferLength that passes this check, leading to a subsequent buffer over-read in copy_to_user().

This assignment directly uses the untrusted server-reported OutputBufferLength without any bounds check against the response buffer size. It sets qi.input_buffer_length to a potentially larger value than the actual data in rsp_iov[1].iov_len, causing copy_to_user() to read beyond the kernel heap buffer and leak adjacent memory.

bic_trace_step.reason: In lines 1458-1470 of the PASSTHRU_QUERY_INFO branch, the code sets qi.input_buffer_length to the server-reported OutputBufferLength (line 1460-1461) without validating that it does not exceed the actual response buffer size (rsp_iov[1].iov_len). Then at line 1467, copy_to_user reads qi.input_buffer_length bytes from qi_rsp->Buffer, which could be beyond the allocated buffer, enabling a heap memory leak. No bounds check against rsp_iov[1].iov_len is present.
